title: Superhero Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Kinobody Hollywood Physique Workout)
summary: NH reworks Kinobody's paywalled superhero program into a three-day upper-body-focused template: Tuesday shoulders and back, Thursday lower body, Saturday chest and arms. He drops reverse pyramid training, keeps rest-pause on last sets and Kinobody's 5 lb progression rule, and adds supersets and neck work. He recommends it for novices and intermediates who want an upper-body-dominant look.
claims: Kinobody is an exception in the aesthetics movement: he writes good training templates, especially for upper body
Reverse pyramid training can waste time and pile up junk volume; use straight sets with the same weight, or variations and back-off sets
Rest-pause on the last set adds reps without hurting performance on the other hard sets
Add 5 lb once you hit the top of the rep range with good form, per Kinobody; small jumps keep momentum and avoid plateaus and resets
Rep standards must stay constant: the first rep's range of motion and speed must match the last, or progress is fake
Tuesday opens with weighted pull-ups (any grip), 3 sets of 5-8, rest-pause last set with 15-30 s rest, superset with abs, calves or neck
Superheroes have thick necks; the original program omitted neck work, which is a mistake
Seated barbell press 3x6-10 supersetted with dumbbell bent-over rows 3x6-12
The upper back thrives on high volume and frequency, even daily; frequent high-rep pressing builds shoulders
Incline dumbbell flies 4x12-15 superset with cable lateral raises 4x10-15; do the chest move first, because fatiguing the shoulder first destabilises the flies and risks rotator cuff tendonitis
Low leg volume opens recovery; training legs every two days as he does creates a lot of fatigue
Bulgarian split squats 3-4x12-15 replace squats because Kinobody thinks squats overbuild the outer quad; unilateral work biases the VMO
Superset the split squats with neck work for 15-20 reps; neck can be trained every session if volume is managed
RDLs 3-4x6-12 are the program's only heavy hinge and can go to failure; if you do not deadlift, do RDLs
Leg extensions 4x15-20 add quad and VMO volume with little fatigue
Dumbbell calf raises 3-4x15-20 and hanging leg raises or ab rollouts; never skip abs, as a developed core is part of the superhero look
Saturday: incline press 3x6-10 with rest-pause last set, superset with abs or neck during the 3-4 minute rest
Seated machine row 3x10-12 antagonist-supersetted with dumbbell bench 3x6-10 or 8-10; dumbbells or a cambered or football bar spare the shoulders
Six to seven weekly chest sets in this day is still within acceptable volume
Optional one-arm cable rows 4x10-12; the upper back absorbs extra work at little recovery cost
Dumbbell incline curls 3-4x6-10 (or 6-8) without bouncing at the bottom, with rope pushdowns 3-4x15-20; swap pushdowns for an overhead extension to hit the long head
High-rep pushdowns should still reach mechanical failure, not just a pump
Three training days keeps frequency low for novices while volume stays higher than typical novice programs
Aesthetic programs must isolate and give more volume to presses; squatting as much as pressing yields a big lower body and lacking upper body
